key_findings: All benchmarks show extreme warmup effects (2-117x slower first run)
Sieve shows deoptimization event at run 6 (40% slowdown)
Two-phase warmup pattern in queens, towers, list suggests tiered compilation

hypotheses.title: Delayed Compilation Threshold Causes Extreme Warmup in Permute
hypotheses.description: The permute benchmark shows a 117x warmup penalty (120ms first run vs 1ms stable). This extreme effect suggests the JIT compiler is not triggering compilation early enough, forcing the first iteration to run in interpreter mode or low-tier compilation.
evidence: Dramatic drop after first iteration suggests tier transition
Pattern indicates interpreter → compiled transition rather than gradual optimization
expected_root_causes: Compilation threshold too high for short-running code
Method call frequency not reaching threshold in single iteration
Possible OSR (On-Stack Replacement) not triggering for loops
Small code size may delay profiling data collection

hypotheses.title: Multi-Phase Warmup Indicates Tiered Compilation Progression
hypotheses.description: Queens, towers, and list show two-phase warmup patterns (run 1 very slow, run 2 moderately slow, run 3+ stable), suggesting progression through GraalVM's compilation tiers.
expected_root_causes: Run 1: Interpreted or minimal profiling
Run 2: Tier 1 compilation (low optimization)
Run 3+: Tier 2 compilation (full optimization with inlining)
Profiling overhead in early runs collecting data for optimization

hypotheses.title: Deoptimization Event in Sieve Run 6 Due to Type Profiling Change
hypotheses.description: Sieve shows an outlier at run 6 (346ms vs 240-255ms typical), suggesting a deoptimization event where optimized code was invalidated and recompiled.
expected_root_causes: Type speculation failure (e.g., integer overflow to double)
Array bounds check assumption violation
Loop unrolling or vectorization assumption invalidated
Hidden class/shape change in object property access

hypotheses.title: Missing Inlining Opportunities Limit Peak Performance
hypotheses.description: After warmup, benchmarks may still have performance headroom if critical functions are not being inlined. The stabilized performance might be suboptimal due to virtual call overhead.
evidence: Post-warmup performance is stable but unknown if optimal
Truffle DSL specialization may not cover all type combinations
Function call overhead in tight loops (especially permute, queens)
expected_root_causes: Polymorphic call sites preventing inlining
Method size exceeding inlining threshold
Recursive calls not optimized
Insufficient call frequency for inlining decisions

hypotheses.title: Bytecode Interpreter Overhead Dominates First Run Performance
hypotheses.description: The universal warmup penalty across all benchmarks suggests the Truffle bytecode interpreter has significant overhead before compilation, with profiling instrumentation adding additional cost.
evidence: ALL benchmarks show first-run penalties (no exceptions)
Warmup factor correlates inversely with benchmark complexity
Complex sieve: 2.4x (more computation, less overhead ratio)
expected_root_causes: Bytecode dispatch overhead in interpreter
Profiling instrumentation collecting type/branch data
Frame materialization for closures/variables
Lack of specialized nodes before profiling feedback
hypotheses.impact: Universal warmup penalty across all benchmarks
